_what: How many calls one sign-in (a personal key, an AI app's grant, or the account itself) may make before it is asked to wait (read-data/verify-every-port-sign-in-call-limits.mjs). A tier's limit counts calls in its period, by sign-in, never by network address. The first rule whose `when` all hold picks the tier: `holds` is an access the person's plan gives, `caller` is what signed in (key, app, account), `approved_by` how an app's grant was approved. A rule with no `when` is the default and must be last. Host plumbing is not here: the rate limiting bindings and their namespace ids belong to the deploy that counts the calls. Ported from the earlier code base's src/sign-in-calls.json (b6ae0ebf815f). Decision source: security-hardening-revocation-and-ingress-2026-10-05.

words.refused: This sign-in made more than {limit} calls in {seconds} seconds. Wait a minute, or ask for several things in one call.
